about.title: Brisbane Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Brisbane sits in a tight corridor where US-101 traffic, Bayshore Boulevard, and Guadalupe Canyon Parkway funnel commuters, freight, and local drivers through the same few miles. Public crash records show 27 injury collisions and 35 injured people in the most recent full year, with Thursday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in the data. That timing lines up with shift changes and school pickups, when traffic is dense and drivers are distracted or rushed. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information can disappear. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results — we simply connect injured Brisbane residents with an independent attorney who can review the details of the crash, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid mistakes that could hurt your claim later.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like Caltrans on US-101 — may be involved. An attorney can help you sort out which deadline applies before you lose the chance to act.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage of blame assigned to you can reduce your recovery. Insurers often use recorded statements to nudge that percentage higher, which is why declining to speak with the other driver's insurer until you've talked to an attorney is worth considering.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your Brisbane crash reviewed. Because California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, understanding the full value of a claim is worth a conversation before settling early.

items.question: What should I do first after a crash on Guadalupe Canyon Parkway or US-101 in Brisbane?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up hours or days later. Try to document the scene with photos, note any witnesses, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've spoken with an attorney. Preserving this evidence early can matter a great deal if the claim is contested later.

items.question: Do I still have a claim if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: Yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover damages even if you were partially responsible, though your recovery may be reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific Brisbane crash.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Brisbane car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government agency was involved, such as a road maintained by Caltrans along US-101. It's best to have your timeline reviewed early so no deadline is missed.
